original_question: If Gamma is a numerical semigroup and width(Gamma) is the difference between its largest and smallest minimal generators, is the first Betti number of the associated graded ring G_Gamma always bounded above by binom(width(Gamma)+1, 2)?
target_in_paper: Section 3 ("Width"), Problem 9, which the paper attributes to Herzog–Stamate [HS14, Conjecture 2.1]. This is the first-Betti-number/defining-ideal bound for the associated graded ring (tangent cone), not the broader higher-Betti-number extension. The needed notation for the associated graded ring and Betti numbers is set in §1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content correctly: it is about a numerical semigroup Γ, its width as the difference between the largest and smallest minimal generators, the associated graded ring G_Γ, and the specific sharp upper bound (wd(Γ)+1 choose 2) for the first Betti number. That matches the paper’s narrow first-Betti/tangent-cone width question rather than a neighboring broader problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
missing_details: The paper fixes an arbitrary field K and forms the local semigroup ring K[[Γ]]; the associated graded ring is G_Γ = gr_m(K[[Γ]]) with respect to its maximal ideal m, not an unspecified graded ring attached to Γ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
To make the width precise, one should write Γ = ⟨n_1,...,n_e⟩ with n_1 < ... < n_e and define wd(Γ) = n_e - n_1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

The first Betti number should be identified as the first total Betti number over a minimal regular presentation of G_Γ as a standard graded K-algebra. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

Equivalently, if G_Γ ≅ K[x_1,...,x_e]/I_Γ^* is a minimal regular presentation, then β_1(G_Γ) = μ(I_Γ^*), the minimal number of generators of the defining ideal of the tangent cone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

The quantifier is universal: the question is whether the inequality holds for every numerical semigroup Γ. There is no asymptotic clause such as "for sufficiently large" in this target problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

To stay faithful to the paper, the question should remain at the first Betti number; the all-Betti-number version is posed separately later in §3 and is therefore broader than your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
refined_question: Let K be a field and let Γ = ⟨n_1,...,n_e⟩ be a numerical semigroup with n_1 < ... < n_e. Define the width by wd(Γ) = n_e - n_1, let R = K[[Γ]] with maximal ideal m, and let G_Γ = gr_m(R) be the associated graded ring. If G_Γ has a minimal regular presentation G_Γ ≅ K[x_1,...,x_e]/I_Γ^*, is it always true that β_1(G_Γ) = μ(I_Γ^*) ≤ (wd(Γ)+1 choose 2)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for every numerical semigroup Γ = ⟨n_1,...,n_e⟩ over a field K, does the defining ideal I_Γ^* of the tangent cone G_Γ = gr_m(K[[Γ]]) require at most (wd(Γ)+1 choose 2) minimal generators? This is equivalent because §1 identifies the first Betti number with the minimal number of generators of the defining ideal in a minimal regular presentation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
justification: Although your instruction template mentions Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3, arXiv:2406.00790 is a survey organized by numbered Problems rather than by those labels. Within this paper, the draft matches §3, Problem 9 most closely: it asks exactly for the explicit width bound on the first Betti number of the associated graded ring (equivalently, on the number of defining equations of the tangent cone). It does not match the interval-completion comparison problems nearby, and it is narrower than the later higher-Betti-number generalization. I therefore sharpened the draft by importing only the paper’s own §1 notation and the exact §3 scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
